summary: Muzaffar Alam is a historian and Indologist who studied at Jamia Millia Islamia, Aligarh Muslim University, and Jawaharlal Nehru University (doctorate). He taught at JNU (~1973–2001) before serving as George V. Bobrinskoy Professor at the University of Chicago from ~2001.

Linguist and Indologist Myles Dillon studied at UCD, Berlin, Bonn (Ph.D.), Heidelberg, and TCD under scholars including Meillet and Thurneysen. He held posts at the Sorbonne, TCD, UCL, Wisconsin-Madison, Chicago, Edinburgh, and served as Director of DIAS (1960–1968).
A scholar of Buddhist studies, Myokyo-ni studied at the University of Graz and trained under traditional teacher Soko Morinaga in 1984.
Myosei Tatsuguchi is a Buddhist studies scholar who served as a professor (attested 1987) and professor emeritus (attested 2015) at Ryukoku University.

Mysore Hiriyanna was an Indologist and philosopher educated at Madras Christian College. He studied under Perisamy Tirumalacharya and Kashi Sesharamasastry, later serving as Professor of Sanskrit at Maharaja's College, Mysore (~1912–1927) and at the University of Mysore (~1916–1927).

Indologist Mysore Narasimhachar Srinivas studied at Mysore, Mumbai (Ph.D. under G. S. Ghurye), and Oxford (D.Phil. under Radcliffe-Brown and Evans-Pritchard). He taught at Oxford, Baroda, Delhi, and chaired the Institute for Social and Economic Change (1972–1979).

Mário Bruno Cruz completed a master's in translation at NOVA University of Lisbon and doctoral coursework at the University of Lisbon. He has worked primarily as an architect and translator for multiple publishing houses and organizations.

Tibetology and religious studies scholar Mélanie Vandenhelsken earned a doctorate from the University of Montpellier. She held positions at Montpellier, the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology, the University of Lille, the University of Vienna, and Webster Vienna Private University.
Mónika Kiss is a scholar in Japanology and Buddhist studies who studied at Eötvös Loránd University under Masanori Yamaji, Robert F. Rhodes, and Nozomu Saito.
Indologist N. A. Gore served as a librarian at the Asiatic Society of Mumbai (attested 1957–1958) and Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar Marathwada University (attested 1967).

N. A. Jayawickrama was an Indologist, linguist, and Buddhist studies scholar who served as a professor at the University of Ceylon (attested 1974) and the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies.

Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar N. Aiyaswami Sastri studied at Madras Sanskrit College and Visva-Bharati University. He held professorships at Sri Venkateswara Oriental College (attested 1940) and Visva-Bharati University (attested 1971).

Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar N. D. Mironov studied at Saint Petersburg, Strasbourg (Ph.D.), Berlin, and Bonn under scholars including Hübschmann, Leumann, and Jacobi. He taught at Moscow State, Saint Petersburg, and Irkutsk State universities, and worked at the Asiatic Museum.
Indologist and linguist N. Ganesan attended Victoria School and the Anglo-Chinese School, and served as Lead Engineer at NASA (attested 1999).
N. J. Karthika, who works in Indology and computational studies, completed a Ph.D. at and held a post at the Indian Institute of Technology Bombay.

N. Lakshminarayana Rao was an Indology and archaeology specialist who served as Government Epigraphist for India at the Archaeological Survey of India and Special Officer (Epigraphy) for the Government of India in 1956.
N. R. Bhatt was an Indologist and religious studies scholar who held posts at the French Institute of Pondicherry and the École française d'Extrême-Orient (attested 1966).

N. S. Ramachandra Murthy is an Indology and history/archaeology scholar who worked as Epigraphy Assistant for Andhra Pradesh's Department of Archaeology and Museums and retired as Professor of Indian History and Archaeology at Sri Venkateswara University.

Indologist and philosopher N. S. Ramanuja Tatacharya was Vice Chancellor of National Sanskrit University (1989–1994) and subsequently served as a researcher at the French Institute of Pondicherry (~1994–2017).
N. Taher is an archaeology scholar who succeeded K. K. Muhammed as head of the Bhopal circle at the Archaeological Survey of India.
